deck: Week 6, and the Kingwood Nazr went from a running joke to a documented phenomenon with timestamps. Sunday night at 7:49, Haroon posted that Asim had "that Brock Purdy magic going for him now" and would win it all, blue-eye emoji attached. Asim's reply came at 8:12: "right after you said this I lost terry, carried off on a stretcher." At 8:02 Bilal demanded Kashir apologize to the retirement community on behalf of Mike Evans. Evans limped to the locker room before halftime. Kashir ran the clock: "Hadn't even been 50 min. Record timing in fact." Elsewhere, Asim beat the last unbeaten team and announced he can now lose every game, Bazaan scored the weekly high and reviewed the stats page with one word ("Fake"), Bilal started four backups and scored 66, Mustafa won again with half a roster, and the formula, which does not watch football, put a 3-3 team at No. 1. I ran it three times. It kept saying Haroon.

teams.biggestDevelopment: No. 1 at 3-3: most points in the league (736.78) and the best all-play record (45-21).

movementReasons.reason: Leads the league in points (736.78) and all-play (45-21)
108.0, streak over; Dobbins started, Tucker 24.2

teams.headline: THE 3-3 FAVORITE
teams.verdict: 108.0, a win, J.K. Dobbins in the lineup, and a formula that does not care about your record put Haroon at No. 1. I ran it three times.
teams.analysis:
Last week we named a Level of Losing after J.K. Dobbins. This week Haroon started him. 12.1 points, a 108.0 to 95.8 win over Naafay, streak over. The Dobbins Level retires with a 1-0 record as a starter, which is more than most of the guys in this league can say about their flex. The flex, by the way, was Tre Tucker, who was on Haroon's bench a week ago and scored 24.2 on Sunday, which produced the single most Naafay sentence of the season: "Ofcourse Tucker would have the game of his life. Luck box 👀." Allen 18.3, Kittle 15.4, Coleman 13.9. Kyren Williams 8.2 against Arizona, which I mention only because every Rams player in this league had a bad night and we'll get to the rest of them.

Now the part you came for. Team Noor is 3-3 and No. 1 on the board, and I want to explain it before the chat does. Haroon has scored 736.78 points, 45 more than anyone else. He is 45-21 against the entire field, the best mark in Kingwood. The model is seventy percent results, and most of "results" is the all-play record and scoring, because that's the part of fantasy football you actually control. Every NBA power ranking on earth will put a .500 team with a +9 point differential ahead of a 10-4 team that wins by one, and nobody writes in. This is that. A 3-3 favorite. (I know. I know. Say it with me: the formula doesn't watch the games.) Arfan is 5-1 and second by 2.3 points, and the gap between them is one Winston start.

About Sunday night. 7:49 PM, Haroon, about Asim: "got that Brock Purdy magic going for him now. He's gonna win it all at the end. Just watch. InshaAllah. No nazr 🧿." Terry McLaurin was carted off the field before the chat finished reading it. "Bro. I even put the blue eye. Damn. My bad." Then, and this is the sincere part, "I just miss my boy Purdy." He does. The ledger says Asim is up 28.32 lineup points on the trade, and Sunday Haroon gets to see his boy in person: DEDDYBABA at Team Noor, the rematch, with Josh Allen on bye. Goff was "on the trading block" Tuesday night. He's the starter Sunday. Against Asim. With Purdy on the other sideline. If you handed me this script I'd send it back for being too on the nose.

teams.biggestDevelopment: First loss, 76.28, with Jameis Winston covering Burrow's bye; Henry 4.5.

movementReasons.reason: 76.28 with Winston at quarterback; first loss
Still 5-1, 44-22 all-play; Burrow back Sunday

teams.headline: THE WINSTON EXPERIENCE
teams.verdict: 76.28 with Jameis Winston at quarterback, a first loss, and a two-point slide to second. He's still 5-1. Nobody panic. (Arfan is panicking.)
teams.analysis:
I flagged it last week: Burrow on bye, no backup quarterback on the roster, and a man who has made six roster moves all season. Wednesday night at 8:28 Arfan added Jameis Winston and dropped Dalton Schultz, and I'd like to tell you it went fine. Winston scored 6.48. Derrick Henry got 4.5 against Cleveland in a game the Ravens lost 10-13 with Tyler Huntley at quarterback (more on Huntley later, he had a better week than Henry). Pollard 7.6, Stevenson 3.6 in the flex, Bowers 9.0. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 19.4 and was the only starter who looked like he belonged on the No. 1 team. 76.28, the second-lowest score of the week, and the undefeated season ends at Asim's hands, which is the part that stings.

The chat did not let it go. Monday morning Asim sent Arfan a GIF and Arfan replied with two words: "Luck box." (He's not wrong, Asim is the luckiest team in the league by the Index. He's also 4-2.) By 10:15 PM Arfan had moved on to "I can't believe I lost to @Asim," followed by a description of Asim as a magic man that I'm translating loosely. Saturday, before any of this, the commissioner had posted an Instagram reel captioned "What you think you're gonna get Vs what y'all are actually gonna get @Arfan." I'm not saying the league office put the Nazr on him. I'm saying the timing is documented.

The board. 5-1, 44-22 against the field, 691.46 points, second in all three to Haroon, and the 70/30 blend puts him second by 2.3. I'm not going to pretend a 5-1 team in second feels right. It doesn't. It also isn't wrong, because the one week Arfan didn't have Burrow he scored 76, and the formula noticed. Burrow's back Sunday at Bazan, possibly against Lamar Jackson, and the ceiling rank stays at two. One more thing, since we're here: the two teams at the top of the board have made six roster moves each. Bazaan has made thirty. There's a lesson in that and I'm certain nobody in this chat will learn it.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Lost 110.82-79.84 with Kyler, Jefferson and St. Brown on bye; all three return Sunday.

movementReasons.reason: 79.84 with three starters on bye, Skattebo 0.0
Kyler, Jefferson and St. Brown all return; 39-27 all-play, third

teams.headline: THREE STARS ON THE COUCH
teams.verdict: 79.84 with Kyler, Jefferson and St. Brown on bye, Skattebo at 0.0 and Aubrey at 1.0. Third in all-play anyway. Everyone's back Sunday. Against the commissioner.
teams.analysis:
Picture the lineup card. Jordan Love at quarterback because Kyler's on bye. Parker Washington and Kendrick Bourne (a 2 AM Wednesday waiver add) at receiver because Jefferson and St. Brown are on bye. Cam Skattebo in the flex, 0.0. Brandon Aubrey, the best kicker in football, 1.0. The Chiefs defense scored 14.0 and was the best player on the team. Love's 20.24 was second. Kashir benched the Texans defense, which scored −2.0, one day after posting "Defense not keeping up tho which is wild" about them, so he at least saw that one coming. Blake Corum had 13.0 on the bench and it wouldn't have mattered; Ivan scored 110.82 and this one was over by the late games.

Kashir spent the week doing what Kashir does, which is narrating the league back to itself. "V weird scoring week." "Standings are crazy rn." "Dam we all back in the race." And Tuesday morning, looking at the table: "Asim/mustafa went from dead last to contention. I luv da game." He also ran the two best bits of the week. First, the Evans affair: Bilal demanded he apologize to the retirement community for doubting Mike Evans, Kashir answered "Bro I was trying to help you. Can't believe we let Ivan fleece you," Evans went down with the Achilles forty-seven minutes later, and Kashir, who has never once let a timestamp go unrecorded, ruled that Bilal was "taking the spot for bad juju." Second, Monday morning, after Asim complimented Mustafa for the second straight week: "Sorry Mustsfa you just got asimed this morning, GL next season." Asimed is a verb now. It'll be in the glossary by November.

The board likes him more than the standings do. 3-3, sixth in ESPN's table, third in all-play at 39-27, 641.66 points, and the formula moves him up to third. The ceiling jumps to three as well, because the roster that takes the field Sunday has Kyler, Jefferson, St. Brown, Love, McBride, Warren and Skattebo on it, and I'd like to see that version lose a game before I believe it can. Sunday is the Sheikh bowl, Chief sheikh at RamBam, and the commissioner's quarterback is on bye. Kashir's isn't. I'm not predicting anything. I'm just noting that a Sheikh is going to be 4-3 on Monday and the chat will be unbearable either way.

teams.headline: NABIL, CAN YOUR GUY STOP
teams.verdict: 113.6 to 111.7 over the trade partner, a third straight win, and a tight end picked up two hours before kickoff scored 12.8. The ledger says the trade is still working. Nabil said so himself.
teams.analysis:
This one came down to Rachaad White on Monday night, which is a sentence nobody drafted in August. RamBam led by a comfortable margin until White, Nabil's RB2, scored a touchdown against the 49ers, and the chat lit up. Mustafa: "Damn that rachaad white touchdown made it interesting." The commissioner: "Nabil can your guy stop." Nabil, at 9:49 PM, with the resignation of a man who's conceded on three separate Mondays this season: "Bro, no way im winning this week..unless rachaard white run for 30-40 yards. He aint like that." He wasn't like that. Final margin: 1.9.

The lineup had a Sunday-morning story in it. At 10:45 AM, with Tyler Warren questionable, RamBam added Hunter Henry off free agency and dropped Kalif Raymond. Warren didn't play. Henry scored 12.8. That's the kind of move that gets you three straight wins and also the kind of move that, if it goes 2.1, gets you a column about overthinking it, so credit where due. Jonathan Taylor 20.1, Daniels 21.0, Golden 19.4, and Egbuka 14.3 in the flex, which is notable because a week ago Egbuka's 14.2 sat on the bench behind Roman Wilson's 0.0. Roman Wilson was dropped Wednesday. Growth. The Giants defense, added the same day for the Bengals' bye, scored 1.0. Less growth. And C.J. Stroud put up 22.98 on the bench, the line Kashir summarized Saturday as "23/31 3td is crazy," which matters because Daniels is on bye next week and Stroud is the plan.

The trade partners played each other, so let's do the ledger out loud. RamBam's side of the Lamb deal scored 25.3 in the lineup Sunday (Taylor and Emanuel Wilson); Bizzy's side scored 11.5 (Lamb, with Chase Brown on bye). The running count is RamBam +38.10, and Monday night, before the White touchdown, Nabil typed "Gg @Rameel glad the trade worked out," which is the first time in Kingwood history a trade partner has conceded the trade on the record. Screenshot it. 3-3, third in the league in points at 644.12, 35-31 against the field, fourth on the board, up two. Sunday is the Sheikh bowl against Kashir with a backup quarterback who just threw for three touchdowns. Fine. We'll see.

teams.headline: THE JUJU HAS BEEN PASSED ON
teams.verdict: 101.46, the last unbeaten team beaten, 4-2 and second in the standings. Also the luckiest team in the league by a full win, and Asim knows it, and he's doing the bit anyway.
teams.analysis:
Sunday night, 8:04 PM: "Mannn I can lose every game now I'm just happy I beat the only undefeated guy left." That's the whole Asim experience in one message. He beat Arfan by 25, Bhayshul Tuten ran for 22.7, Purdy threw for 17.36, RJ Harvey added 13.1 from the flex, the Broncos and Fairbairn 11.0 each. And then, eight minutes later: "Damn right after you said this I lost terry, carried off on a stretcher." Terry McLaurin was in Asim's lineup. He finished with 3.2, a cart ride and a Tuesday MRI, and the early word from Washington is that his season is probably over. Asim's follow-up was "Haroon knew what he was doing lol jk," and then a GIF captioned "I Can't tell what's real and what's nazr," and honestly, same.

I need to flag something for the scientists. Saturday morning Bilal posted "@Asim tuten is killing it." Sunday, Tuten scored 22.7. No injury. Haroon complimented Asim's quarterback and a receiver went down. Bilal complimented Ivan's receiver and the receiver went down. Bilal complimented Asim's running back and the running back had the best game of his life. The Nazr, as far as I can tell from six weeks of data, only works on wide receivers. I don't make the rules. I just log them. Asim, Monday morning, after complimenting Mustafa for the second straight week: "I don't have the juju anymore it's been passed on." The Juju is a transferable asset. Someone put it on the trade tracker.

The board, and this one's the desk's call. 4-2, second in the standings, winner of three straight. Also 26-40 against the field, tenth, with the second-lowest points-against in the league (553.48) and a Luckbox Index of +1.64, the highest in Kingwood. Kashir pointed out the top two in the standings have the two lowest points-against; Asim's reply was "That's why we're at the top bro," which is either a joke or a philosophy. The formula had him seventh. I'm putting him fifth, because he's 4-2 and he beat the 5-0 team and a model that ranks a 4-2 team seventh needs to look at the standings page once in a while. The trade ledger is +28.32 over Haroon. He has exactly the same points as Bazaan, 618.78, which Asim greeted with "Mashallah." Sunday he's at Team Noor, Allen on bye, Purdy on the field. Last week the quote was "I need Bucky to turn into Josh Allen again." He got Tuten instead. He'll take it.

teams.headline: THE STAFFORD RULE MOVES TO TOKYO
teams.verdict: 79.64, a loss to RN, Trevor Lawrence's 27.34 on the bench and MarShawn Lloyd's 1.0 in the flex. Still 4-2. Still the lowest points-against in the league.
teams.analysis:
For five weeks the Stafford Rule belonged to Bilal: the quarterback on your bench outscores the one you started. This week it emigrated. Yaseen started Bryce Young, who was fine (19.84), and left Trevor Lawrence on the bench, where he scored 27.34 in a Jaguars loss. That alone doesn't lose you the game. MarShawn Lloyd in the flex does. Lloyd scored 1.0. Luther Burden (13.5) and Stefon Diggs (13.4) sat behind him, and either one wins the game by nine. Sunday night, before the final was in, Yaseen posted to Bilal: "You can have marshawn Lloyd also." I think he meant it as a joke. By Tuesday it read like a confession. Add Harold Fannin's 1.4 at tight end and a kicker, Blake Grupe, who was added Wednesday morning, tore his ACL Sunday and was dropped Tuesday at 7:45 AM. One week. He was on the roster for one week.

The chat gave Yaseen the week's best stat and he knew exactly what to do with it. Tuesday morning: "insane that I'm tied for second and he's tied for last. Real luck box lol." The "he" is Ivan. Gang Green has scored 602.24 points this season; I Eat Ass has scored 602.74. Half a point apart. One is 4-2 and the other is 2-4, and Yaseen's explanation was theological: "That's what's happens when you have no hate in your heart. And no Nazr given bro." Then the plan, stated plainly: "Just need to sneak into the playoffs and take it from there." Kashir's read: "Yassen playing it smart siding with Asim so he can avoid the bad juju." Bilal, when told to get the hate out of his heart: "I got alot of hate! So does @Ivan!!!" I love everyone in this paragraph.

The board. 4-2, third in the standings, 28-38 against the field, tenth in points, and 538.56 points allowed, the lowest in the league. The Luckbox Index has him at +1.45, second only to Asim. The formula says eighth. The desk says sixth, right behind Asim, because 4-2 is 4-2 and because the Tokyo waiver wire (eleven moves and counting) keeps finding bodies. He drops three spots from third, and the ceiling slips to eight. Sunday is Team MBK at Gang Green, the two luckiest and unluckiest men in the league in one box score, and Josh Jacobs is eligible to come back for it. Lloyd will be on the bench. I'm almost sure of it.

teams.headline: FOUR BACKUPS
teams.verdict: 66.68, the week's low, three straight losses, 2-4. Bilal started Stafford for the first time all year and Stafford outscored Dak. The Rule survives on a technicality.
teams.analysis:
Gibbs, Higgins and LaPorta on bye. Jacobs on IR. Judkins questionable, didn't play. Tank Dell on IR. Bilal's own description: "I had 4 backups playing." He was underselling it. The starting lineup had Audric Estime (added Sunday morning at 11:02), Pat Freiermuth (added Wednesday at 3:48 AM), KC Concepcion, Wan'Dale Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr., who scored 7.9, 2.1, 5.9, 3.7 and 2.0. Matt Gay, also added Wednesday, kicked 12.0 and was the second-best player on the team. And the Stafford Rule in Week 6 took a turn: Bilal finally started Matthew Stafford. Stafford scored 16.88. Dak scored 11.02 on the bench. He got it right. It didn't matter. The Stafford Rule is hereby amended: whichever quarterback Bilal starts will be the correct one, and he will lose by fifty anyway.

Bilal's Law, delivered Sunday at 8:48 PM, is the best thing anyone wrote this week: "There are two things you need to know about this league! Everyone who wins in this league is a luckbox and all trades are scams!" Mustafa: "fax." It's going in the methodology page. He also ran the Evans affair from the other side, demanding Kashir "apologize to the retirement community for Evan's! He still got it!" and then, after the Achilles, "You didn't say sorry!!!" The trade ledger does not help his case. Evans has scored 33.7 in two weeks for Ivan; Judkins has 6.5 for Bilal and a 0.0 Sunday. Bilal, to Ivan: "you got more pts from Evan's than judkins for sure!" Kashir: "Can't believe we let Ivan fleece you." Kashir again, as consolation: "Dw you got Josh Jacob's comin back. Should be a come up." Bilal on Jacobs: "Next week! InshAllah." The NFL says Jacobs is eligible Sunday. The Packers say his status is to be determined. The desk says he's a Week 7 flex with a question mark and the rest is between Bilal and the universe.

The board drops him to seventh, and the Luckbox Index has a bottom and it's him. 2-4 at 36-30 against the field. 649.72 points scored, third in the league. 735.32 points allowed, the most in the league. Minus 1.27 wins of luck. He's scored more than Arfan and he's 2-4. (That one took me a minute too.) Sunday he's at Yaseen with Gibbs, Higgins and LaPorta back and maybe Jacobs. Bilal, Monday, when Kashir blamed his juju for the 2-4: "Oh yeah! You got me! Thats why I'm 2-4 🤦🏽‍♂️." It's the byes, Bilal. It's always been the byes.

teams.biggestDevelopment: 111.7 and lost by 1.9; Loveland 15.5 sat behind Higbee's 2.2.

movementReasons.reason: 111.7 and lost by 1.9; Loveland 15.5 and Shough 26.96 on the bench
Walker 26.9, Maye 23.8, Lamb back; 646.04 points, fourth

teams.headline: THE DOBBINS LEVEL, TRADE PARTNER EDITION
teams.verdict: 111.7, the fifth-best score of the week, and a 1.9-point loss to the guy he traded with. Loveland 15.5 and Shough 26.96 on the bench. The Dobbins Level has its second member.
teams.analysis:
The Dobbins Level, for those joining late: you lose by less than a guy on your bench scored. Nabil qualifies twice. Colston Loveland scored 15.5 on the bench while Tyler Higbee, added Wednesday afternoon, scored 2.2 at tight end. Tyler Shough scored 26.96 on the bench while Drake Maye, who is having a real season, scored 23.8. I don't blame the Maye call. I blame the Higbee call, and Nabil probably does too, because the margin was 1.9 and Loveland alone wins it by thirteen. The rest of the lineup was good! Kenneth Walker scored 26.9 in his first week back from bye, Rachaad White had 13.7 with the Monday night touchdown, Keenan Allen (a 2 AM Wednesday waiver claim) scored 12.2, and CeeDee Lamb returned at 11.5. 111.7 wins eight of the twelve matchups this week. It didn't win this one.

Nabil's concession timing is now a tracked stat. Last week he conceded at 11:54 AM Sunday. This week he waited until 9:29 PM Monday: "Gg @Rameel glad the trade worked out." Then White scored, Mustafa posted "that rachaad white touchdown made it interesting," and Nabil, at 9:49, retracted nothing: "no way im winning this week..unless rachaard white run for 30-40 yards. He aint like that." He had the score right. Also this week: Will Shipley dropped after the partial plantar tear, Deebo still out, Ty Johnson added and dropped within a day. The waiver wire in New York is a revolving door and Nabil's standing in it.

The ledger reads RamBam +38.10 after the trade partners' head-to-head, which Nabil has now endorsed in writing. The board barely moves: 2-4, 32-34 against the field, 646.04 points, fourth in the league, and eighth on the board for a second straight week. Maye and Walker are a real foundation. Collins at 9.4 and Higbee at 2.2 are not. Sunday he's at RN, which two weeks ago would have been a layup and now means Mustafa, who's won two straight with a lineup card that looks like a hospital intake form. Nobody is a layup anymore. That was the week's lesson, and Nabil learned it by 1.9.

Lamar targeted for Week 7; Cook, Swift and Nabers all over 21

teams.headline: THE HUNDO AT THIRTY MOVES
teams.verdict: 116.4, the weekly high, the $100 check, and the most roster moves in the league. Tyler Huntley, picked up Thursday, started over Lamar Jackson and Aaron Rodgers. It worked.
teams.analysis:
Let me read you Bazaan's transaction log, because it's a genre now. Tuesday, 9:44 to 9:49 AM: dropped Isaac TeSlaa, the Cowboys defense (the −2.0 from last week), Chad Ryland and Antonio Williams. Wednesday: added Nick Folk. Thursday: added Tyler Huntley. Saturday, 7:03 AM: added Ja'Kobi Lane and Seth McGowan. Tuesday morning after the win, 6:16 AM: dropped Folk, who kicked 1.0. Thirty moves on the season, the most in the league by seven. The Bazaan Transaction Rate is holding at five a week with scattered showers. And it worked! Huntley, starting for Baltimore with Lamar still out, scored 13.4 while Lamar (0.0) and Rodgers (16.02) sat. Cook 22.8, Nabers 22.5, Swift 21.0, Dameon Pierce 13.0 in the flex because Philadelphia's backfield is a Bazaan waiver claim right now, Coker 12.7, the Ravens 10.0. Juwan Johnson 0.0 at tight end and Folk's 1.0 were the only misses, and he still won the week.

116.4 is the weekly high, which is good news for Bazaan ($100, now down $267 instead of $367) and a mild indictment of everyone else, because it's the lowest weekly high of the season by seventeen points. Kashir's "V weird scoring week" covers it. Bazaan's own week in the chat: "Mannn just wait till my team healthy @thedepartment" on Tuesday, "Fake" at 1:43 AM Wednesday in response to the stats page, and Tuesday morning, the observation of the week: "Me n Asim have the exact same pts scored." They do. 618.78 each. Asim is 4-2 and second. Bazaan is 3-3 and seventh. Asim said "Mashallah." Bazaan did not.

The board moves him up one, to ninth, with the ceiling up to nine, because the Ravens are targeting Lamar for Sunday and a lineup with Lamar, Cook, Swift and Nabers in it has a December in it. Two things cut the other way. James Cook is on bye Sunday, against Arfan, and Adonai Mitchell, the return for Bryce Young, has now scored 0.0 in four straight weeks for Bazaan with a status tag of "D," which I assume stands for doubtful but could be a grade. The ledger reads Gang Green +54.94 on that one. Bazaan's season, for the record: 33-33 against the field, a Luckbox Index of exactly 0.00. The only man in the league whose record is precisely what he's earned. Somehow that's the least Bazaan stat imaginable.

Second straight loss, 2-4

teams.headline: THE SECOND NEGATIVE DEFENSE
teams.verdict: 95.8, a second straight loss, a second straight −2.0 from a defense, and Davante Adams gone for six to ten weeks. Caleb's back, at least.
teams.analysis:
Last week the Bears defense scored −2.0 for Naafay, so at 2:41 AM Thursday he dropped them and claimed the Jaguars defense off waivers. The Jaguars scored −2.0. Two different defenses, two different weeks, same number. That's not a slump. That's a brand. The rest of the lineup was fine: Kyle Pitts 20.5 (yes, really, it's a Falcons tight end renaissance and I'm as confused as you), Metcalf 14.8, Javonte 12.0, Butker 12.0 in his first week after Naafay cut Jake Bates, and Caleb Williams, back from injury, 16.5. Bijan Robinson scored 6.3 against the Bears and Alvin Kamara had 13.9 on the bench, and I'm not going to pretend starting Bijan was wrong, because it wasn't, and it still cost him. Deshaun Watson, the fill-in quarterback, was dropped Tuesday at 1:13 PM, an hour before the screenshots. Caleb's the guy.

The loss was to Haroon, which produced a lament for the ages: "I can never beat Haroon mannn lmao." He's not wrong; Naafay has now lost to Team Noor in the only two meetings this season, including Week 2, and Sunday's version came with Tre Tucker's 24.2 from Haroon's flex, which Naafay greeted with "Ofcourse Tucker would have the game of his life. Luck box 👀." Then the news. Davante Adams scored 5.4, left the Rams game late, and Monday Sean McVay said he'd miss six to ten weeks with a ruptured hamstring tendon. For a roster that's already got Jordan Mason and Jadarian Price on IR, that's the third running back or receiver gone, and the second starting receiver.

The board drops him three, to tenth, and the ceiling falls from nine to ten, on Adams. The numbers are sturdier than the rank: 2-4 but 33-33 against the field, 633.84 points, right at the league average, a Luckbox Index of −1.00 (unlucky, but not Bilal unlucky). The formula had him ninth; the desk went Bazan over IVaafay on the Lamar news. Sunday is at I Eat Ass, 2-4 against 2-4, and the loser is 2-5 with Pickens, Pitts and Caleb on one side and McCaffrey and Cousins on the other. I'm not ready to write that column. Somebody's going to make me.

teams.headline: ASIMED
teams.verdict: 83.78 beats 79.64. Two straight wins with Barkley and Moore out and two Vikings on bye. Mustafa is 3-3. Asim complimented him again Monday morning. Hold on to something.
teams.analysis:
Here's the Week 6 lineup for the team that's won two straight: Mahomes, back from bye, 10.48. Omarion Hampton 5.9. Kendre Miller, a 2:11 AM Wednesday waiver claim, 8.0. DeVonta Smith 17.0. Ladd McConkey, questionable, 2.2. Travis Kelce 7.3. The Colts defense, added Wednesday at 3:18 AM and dropped Tuesday at 4:32 AM, 5.0. Jason Myers, added Wednesday at 3:21 AM, 7.0. And Isaiah Likely, 20.9, a week after 26.9, which means the best tight end in Kingwood over the last two weeks is Isaiah Likely and I'm not taking questions. Germie Bernard, added Wednesday at 3:34 AM, scored 20.2 on the bench. RN made twenty-three moves this season, second only to Bazaan, and four of them happened between 2:11 and 3:34 one Wednesday morning. Say what you want about the roster. The man is awake.

And then Monday morning happened. Asim, 8:24 AM: "Ppl sleepin on Mustafa his team all banged up yet still pulled off 2 dubs mA." Kashir, three minutes later: "Sorry Mustsfa you just got asimed this morning, GL next season." Asim, defending himself: "I was the only one who complimented him last week and he got another dub this week. I don't have the juju anymore it's been passed on." So the official Kingwood position is that the Juju is a transferable asset, Asim no longer holds it, and Mustafa is the control group that proves it. Mustafa's contribution to the discourse was co-signing Bilal's Law ("fax") and holding his ground when the chat started a whole bit about who's a capbox and who's a faxbox. He's a faxbox. His words.

The board, and it's the desk's call again. 3-3 and eighth in the standings, but 19-47 against the field and 558.44 points, both the worst in the league, and a Luckbox Index of +1.27. The formula says twelfth. I'm keeping him eleventh over Ivan, same as last week and for the same reason: the team that wins with this lineup card has earned one rung, and the roster that shows up when Barkley and DJ Moore are back is not the roster that's 19-47. Doubs went to IR this week, which hurts, and Barkley still has no date. Sunday it's Bizzy at RN. Two weeks ago I ranked this roster twelfth and it's won twice since, which is either the Nazr or a flaw in the model, and I'm not ruling out both.

teams.headline: AT LEAST EVANS CAUGHT IT
teams.verdict: 110.82, the first win since Week 1, McCaffrey 26.2. Then Jalen Hurts' season ended, Mike Evans limped off, and Ivan's own post about it had a crying emoji. Correctly.
teams.analysis:
Start with the good part, because there was one. Ivan scored 110.82, the third-best total of the week, and beat Kashir by 31. Christian McCaffrey ran for 26.2 against Washington. Kirk Cousins, starting because of the Hurts news, threw for 18.52. The Steelers defense 11.0, Olave 12.3, Mike Evans 10.9 before he left. Carnell Tate had 16.0 on the bench and Tanner McKee, a Saturday add who is now Philadelphia's starting quarterback, had 12.6. It's the first win since Week 1, five weeks of losing ended, and it moved Ivan from 1-4 to 2-4, which in this standings table is the difference between "last" and "tied with three other guys." Kashir: "Dam we all back in the race." Ivan is included in that. Barely, but included.

Now the rest. Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve this week and is expected to miss the remainder of the season for medical reasons. That's the last sentence this column will spend on it, except to say the desk wishes him a full recovery. For Ivan it means Cousins is the quarterback the rest of the way, with McKee as the backup plan, and a roster that drafted Hurts to be the ceiling now has a ceiling made of Kirk Cousins. Then, Monday night: Mike Evans limped to the locker room before halftime with Achilles soreness. Shanahan says the tendon's intact and it won't need more testing; the beat says he probably misses a little time. The chat, naturally, had already assigned blame. Bilal's "He still got it!" went up at 8:02. Kashir logged the injury at 8:49. Ivan's own verdict, with the only appropriate emoji: "At least Evan's caught it 🥲." On the running backs he and Bilal swapped, Montgomery and Judkins, both 0.0 Sunday: "Both our RBs chillin lol."

The ledger says I Eat Ass +27.20 over Team MBK on that trade, and Bilal said it out loud: "Ivan you got more pts from Evan's than judkins for sure!" The board doesn't move much. 2-4, 26-40 against the field, 723.8 points allowed (second-most), and the formula has him eleventh. The desk keeps him twelfth behind Mustafa, because the ceiling just went from Hurts to Cousins and the ceiling rank drops to twelve with it. Sunday is IVaafay at I Eat Ass, 2-4 against 2-4, and Bilal has already announced the stakes: "I got alot of hate! So does @Ivan!!!" Hate, per Yaseen, is what keeps you out of the playoffs. Ivan's going to need a lot of McCaffrey.
